title: Acute severe asthma, 32-year-old woman
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Worsening shortness of breath and wheeze since this morning; can only speak in short phrases.
intake.history: Known asthmatic. Uses salbutamol inhaler; ran out of her preventer inhaler two weeks ago.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 2. A: Primary triage Respiratory Distress p4: 'Difficulty to breathe', 'Short phrases only', 'SpO2 90 - 92% room air' are in the x~246 column = Level 2 (SpO2 91%, short phrases). Adult vitals p7: 'SpO2 < 92%' is Level 2 (x~131); HR 118 ('HR 100 - 120') and RR 30 ('RR 20 - 30') are Level 3 (x~244). Complaint lists: SOB p11 'Wheeze, expiratory rhonchi; airway intact' and RESPIRATORY p10 'Wheezing, known asthmatic' are Level 3 (x~244). Most urgent applicable = Level 2. Level 1 criteria (cannot speak / one-word replies, SpO2 < 90%, confused/lethargic, needs assisted breathing) are absent; re-triage if she deteriorates. B: SpO2 91% is in the Level 2 cell 'SpO2 < 92%' (adult vital signs p7, x~131). Primary triage respiratory distress Level 2 cells (p4, x~246): 'Difficulty to breathe', 'Short phrases only', 'SpO2 90 - 92% room air'. HR 118 and RR 30 are only Level 3 ('HR 100 - 120', 'RR 20 - 30', p7 x~244); RR is exactly 30, not > 30. Complaint 'Wheezing, known asthmatic' is Level 3 (p10, x~244). No Level 1 feature: not one-word replies, not SpO2 < 90%, not confused (p4, x~136). If the 91% was measured on oxygen rather than room air, the level does not change.

disposition.note: Initial treatment in the ED critical zone (Level 2), then admission for severe asthma. ICU/HDU if poor response, hypercapnia or life-threatening features. Discharge is not acceptable: the CPG requires admission for severe exacerbations. / Severe exacerbation (RR > 25) means admission. ICU/HDU if she responds poorly, tires, or has hypercapnia or worsening hypoxaemia.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Severity grading: RR 30 (>25/min) is a 'severe' parameter; HR 118, SpO2 91% and speaking in phrases are 'moderate'. The CPG says to classify by the most severe parameter, giving severe. A report calling it moderate is listed only as a weak alternative.

The QR algorithm's severity headers for the mild/moderate and severe columns are graphics without extractable text. The severe-column drug list (x~186: SABA via O2-driven nebuliser, ipratropium 0.5 mg stat, IV hydrocortisone 100 mg, IV MgSO4 2 g) was assigned by x-position; only 'LIFE THREATENING' (x~241) is printed as text.
Non-selective beta-blockers are described only as 'can exacerbate asthma' / use with caution, not as contraindicated, so they are not listed as forbidden.
B: Severity is mixed: RR 30 (> 25/min) is in the Severe column, but speech in phrases, HR 118 and SpO2 91% are in the Moderate column. Table 9 says to classify by the most severe parameter, which gives 'severe'. The Table 9 quote comes from column-flattened text, so the column headers do not sit next to the cells.
IV magnesium is marked required because Recommendation 12 names acute severe asthma, but the wording is 'should be considered'.
